linkedin.hook: The Curve collateral crisis exposed why pooled lending models fail institutional risk frameworks.
linkedin.copy:
Michael Egorov's reliance on OTC counterparties to prevent a cascading liquidation on Curve revealed an uncomfortable truth about DeFi credit. In pooled collateral markets, every passive LP inadvertently underwrites the risk profile of the largest borrower. When a massive position approaches liquidation, execution latency and market depth evaporate, leaving protocols with bad debt that gets socialized across depositors.

Institutional capital requires deterministic risk boundaries. On Stellar Soroban, Vanna replaces shared risk pools with isolated SmartAccount sandboxes. Borrowers manage leverage and collateral inside discrete execution environments, completely separated from core liquidity vaults. If a borrower position deteriorates, liquidation triggers automatically at a 1.10x Health Factor floor. The borrower's collateral takes the hit inside their sandbox, while passive lenders remain shielded from systemic contagion.

Underwriting safety also depends on settlement speed. Relying on ~320ms Mercury indexer state updates and 0.00014 XLM fixed gas costs, liquidators on Soroban can close distressed balances before slippage eats into capital. Manual bailouts and backroom deals are structural bugs, not features. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to review the contract architecture.

reddit.hook: Why shared-pool lending models like Curve need OTC bailouts and how Soroban sandboxes solve it
reddit.copy:
Watching Michael Egorov scramble to arrange off-market OTC deals to avoid liquidating his CRV position on Aave and other venues highlighted the systemic risk of pooled debt.

In standard pooled money markets, risk is fungible. If a borrower deposits an illiquid token or builds a position so large that on-chain liquidity cannot absorb the liquidation, every passive LP in the pool bears that tail risk. If keepers cannot liquidate quickly enough due to gas price spikes or frontrunning, the pool accrues bad debt. You saw this play out in real time where the protocol was essentially held hostage by an outsized debt balance.

We approached credit design on Stellar Soroban with a hard boundary model using isolated SmartAccount sandboxes.

Instead of dumping collateral into a unified pool, each borrower spins up an isolated SmartAccount instance. Passive LPs supply capital to a core pool governed by strict risk parameters, but leverage execution happens strictly inside the user's dedicated contract sandbox. Cross-collateralization between disparate positions does not exist.

Liquidations trigger at a fixed 1.10x Health Factor floor. Because state synchronization runs on ~320ms Mercury indexer latency and transactions clear at 0.00014 XLM fixed network fees, keeper bots do not get priced out by gas wars during volatile downswings. The debt clears inside the sandbox without socialized haircut mechanics hitting passive depositors.

If you want to test the contract mechanics yourself, you can deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Disclosure: I am an engineer building core credit infrastructure at Vanna Protocol on Stellar.
